title: VibeGraph quality layer: quality model
description: Dimensions of code quality, each with a prose half (the why), a checks half (verbs from check_grammar.json), an applies_when predicate over the stack profile, an evidence class, a mode, and a threshold and calibration that are Unknown until Run 3 measures them. Three things are enforced by shape rather than by convention: every dimension names at least one profile fact in applies_when (there is no `always`, because a universal rule set applied everywhere is the named failure mode); every check binding names the Run 1 assertions that forced it (an unforced check does not exist); and a gate-blocking dimension must carry a calibration record, so nothing gates before it has discriminated on this repository's own history. The five dimension ids are the five Run 1 verbs' outcomes; adding one is a schema change with its own review, which is how the catalogue cap holds without a count.

DimensionId.description: One per Run 1 verb outcome. boundary-integrity: guards, callers-only, import-only, calls-through. failure-visibility: handles-failure. repetition-cost: not-in-loop. resolvability: annotated. change-coupling: co-changes.

AssertionId.description: A Run 1 assertion id (RUN1.md section 1) or a stated constraint id.

Predicate.description: Over the stack profile. Composable with all/any/not. A leaf names a fact and a value it has or asserts the fact is absent, or names a regime tag. No `always`.

Measurement.description: A measured pair, only ever written by Run 3 calibration against a named commit. The place numbers are allowed to exist.

CalibrationRecord.description: A check earns its place only by discriminating across known-good and known-bad code drawn from this repository's own defect history. The record names the sample, the fire rate, the human false-positive review and the commit, so a stale calibration is visible.

samplesFrom.description: Run 3: the candidate file holding each sampled unit's id, label, source and raw verdict (scripts/quality_calibrate.mjs). The record keeps the NodeRefs; the detail lives there.

falsePositiveReview.description: Who judged the fires on good or presumed-good code, and how each was judged. A human, or a model the human DELEGATED to (Ben's ruling of 2026-09-12: the agent pipeline runs with the human out of the loop; RUN3.md section 10). A model review names the model and the ruling that delegated it, and carries every judgement with its reason, so it is never mistaken for a human's. Three verdicts per fire: false-positive (the verb is wrong here), finding (the label was wrong; the code has the defect), intended (the shape is real and the author meant it: wants a stated allowance, not a verb change). Only false-positive demotes.

model.description: Required when reviewedBy is model: the audit label, e.g. claude:claude-fable-5-1.

delegatedBy.description: Required when reviewedBy is model: the human ruling that delegated the review.

notes.description: One entry per fire on good, presumed-good or neutral code. Never empty when such fires exist.

Threshold.description: Only meaningful beside a calibration. Run 2 instances carry Unknown here.

forcedBy.description: The Run 1 assertions that forced the verb. Never empty.

text.description: The prose half: the why a worker reads.

evidenceClass.description: A: IR-decidable. B: needs the trace overlay, a build artefact or a test run. C never enters the model; a qualitative judgement goes to a model with provenance model_judgement and never into a gate.
